newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HODDLE TO SPEAK TO TROUBLED MIDFIELDER GASCOIGNE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODDLE TO SPEAK TO TROUBLED MIDFIELDER GASCOIGNE.

text.p: England manager Glenn Hoddle will speak to his troubled midfielder Paul Gascoigne after a traumatic 24 hours for the man he said recently could figure in his plans for the next six years.
Gascoigne, 29, was sent off in the first half of Glasgow Rangers' European Cup Champions' League match against Ajax in Amsterdam on Wednesday.
The following morning British newspapers published pictures of his wife Sheryl with a bruised face and her left arm in a sling. Neither Gascoigne or his wife have commented.

"Glenn Hoddle is obviously concerned about the events of the past 24 hours," said Football Association director of public affairs David Davies on Friday. "He will speak to Paul when the time is right."
Rangers' manager Walter Smith gave qualified support on Thursday for Gascoigne, who will miss the return match on October 30 and could be banned for at least two further European games.

"I will have to talk with him to see if I consider he can handle playing without over-reacting in the manner he did on Wednesday," Smith said. "There has to be a limit to anybody's patience. Understanding can only go so far."
Rangers bought Gascoigne from Italian club Lazio for 4.3 million pounds sterling ($6.8 million) with the express intention of succeeding in Europe.
But after losing 4-1 to Ajax they remain bottom of their group and effectively have no chance of advancing further after Gascoigne's second sending off in two seasons.
A born-again Christian who succeeded Terry Venables as England manager following Euro 96, Hoddle is a man of strong moral views who is committed to improving England's off-the-field image.
Ten days ago Hoddle said he had had a frank talk with Gascoigne as England prepared for their World Cup qualifier against Poland and been impressed with his attitude.
"Paul can go on playing longer than he might have thought he could," Hoddle said. "I believe he can go on until he's 35 at least, this World Cup and, yes, another."
English bookmakers William Hill have turned down requests to quote odds on Gascoigne getting a red card in Rangers' match against Aberdeen this weekend.
But they have reported lively interest in their new betting market on which country Gascoigne will be playing in next season.
He is a 4-7 favourite to stay in Scotland but William Hill will also give 200-1 odds on his playing in Albania or San Marino.
